title: Chapter 11
content:
The place Kang Seok-joo brought him to was crammed with decrepit, crumbling low-rises. Tucked far away from the bustling neon avenues, the run-down commercial district was lined with row after row of shuttered storefronts plastered with faded For Lease signs. The narrow alleyways tangled together like a spider's web, but winding deep into the labyrinth led to a single building that was surprisingly well-maintained.

There were no security cameras mounted outside, no casual pedestrians strolling by—only a pair of hulking bouncers standing guard at the reinforced entrance.

Why on earth are filthy-rich trust fund brats partying in a slum like this?

The second Jakyeong stepped through the heavy threshold, the question evaporated.

In stark contrast to the dilapidated exterior, the underground level was an entirely different universe. The interior decor and ambient lighting were opulent enough to rival high-end Gangnam clubs, while the deafening, bass-heavy EDM sent vibrations straight through the floor, kicking the pulse into overdrive.

Thick, hazy clouds of tobacco and cannabis smoke hung suspended in the air. Decadent, drug-addled youth danced and sprawled across leather loungers without an ounce of shame, stripped down to bare skin and tangled in half-naked heaps.

Pushing through a shimmering curtain of gold metal beads, Jakyeong found a heated indoor plunge pool nestled deeper inside. Men and women splashed together in the water, completely lost in a haze of drunken laughter.

"Our brand-new private hideout," Seok-joo whispered, leaning his mouth right against Jakyeong’s ear with a sleazy chuckle. "Even Executive Director Kang doesn't know this place exists."

Having decided they were best buddies after sharing a bribe, the kid had already demoted his brother from "Second Brother" to "Executive Director Kang."

Past the pool and up a shallow flight of stairs sat an elevated VIP lounge furnished with curved leather sofas and low glass tables. A pack of Seok-joo’s degenerate friends spotted them, waving their arms in raucous greeting. Several of them already had fine white powder dusted across their nostrils, pupils blown wide as they drifted somewhere between euphoria and oblivion.

The moment Jakyeong took a seat, the room's attention pivoted entirely away from Seok-joo and locked onto him.

"Who’s this? A guest?"

"Wait, is this the friend who flew in from Hong Kong?"

"Look at those glasses. People still wear frames like that?"

A girl perched nearby—wearing microscopic denim shorts and an unclasped bikini top—stared shamelessly at Jakyeong.

"You're gorgeous," she purred, leaning in until her generous cleavage was pressed flush against his shoulder. "Why hide behind these nerd specs? Take them off. Want me to take them off for you?"

As she reached to pluck the glasses from his face, Jakyeong leaned back, gently catching her wrist and guiding it away.

"No, I'm fine, thank you."

"Aww, look at him blushing! That’s so fucking cute."

Seeing the girl openly fawn over Jakyeong, Seok-joo let out a loud snicker. "Hey, keep your paws off him. His grandfather is a terrifying old bastard."

"More terrifying than your brother?"

The mention of Kang Il-hyun caused the circle to erupt in mocking laughter. Seok-joo’s face, however, instantly curdled into a scowl like he’d swallowed a mouthful of shit.

"Shut your crazy fucking mouth, bitch. Why bring that psycho up?"

Jakyeong didn't need to ask to know "that psycho" meant Kang Il-hyun.

While Seok-joo sat there fuming, a heavily built man ambled over. He wore a black beanie, with a grotesque dokkaebi goblin tattoo snaking across his entire left arm. Jakyeong stared at the ink—something about the design struck a faint chord of familiarity.

The man introduced himself as Choi Ki-tae. After exchanging a few hushed whispers with Seok-joo, Ki-tae moved to a discreet side table and pulled a small ziplock bag from inside his jacket. He dropped a few pills onto a flat ceramic tile, expertly crushed them into a fine dust, blended the result with an existing mound of white powder, and slid the prepared line toward Seok-joo.

Without a second's hesitation, Seok-joo bent down, plugged one nostril, and snorted the line with a violent inhale.

Moments later, his jaw dropped slack, his eyes rolling back until only the whites were showing. Trembling all over like a man in the throes of an orgasm, he melted into the plush sofa. One by one, the rest of the circle crowded in to take their turns.

As Jakyeong watched the freak show with a detached, deadpan expression, a flute of champagne was thrust into his line of sight. Pale golden liquid bubbled softly against the crystal rim.

The girl who had tried to snatch his glasses earlier was smiling down at him. "Drink up. It'll put you in the right mood."

Jakyeong offered a polite smile and shook his head. Drinking an open beverage from a stranger in a drug den was a fast track to waking up in a ditch.

Unfazed, the girl set the glass onto the table and slid closer, threading her bare arm through his and leaning her upper body against him. With a heady wave of sweet perfume, she brazenly rubbed her full chest against his bicep. Jakyeong managed an awkward, timid chuckle.

"You're a lot firmer than you look."

Her hand drifted from his arm, sliding over the hard planes of his chest, down his abdomen, and dipping lower still. Right through the fabric of his trousers, her fingers stroked over his crotch.

She held his gaze, leaning in to capture his mouth in a kiss.

Jakyeong caught her hand, peeled it away, and pushed himself up from the sofa.

The girl’s brow twitched in annoyance.

"I'm terribly sorry," Jakyeong stammered, putting on his best frail persona. "My lungs aren't very strong... I need to step out for a breath of fresh air."

She caught his wrist. "Want me to come with you?"

Jakyeong slipped his arm from her grip a second time. Having a girl rub him like that after months of dry spells certainly stirred his instincts, but getting distracted was out of the question right now. Flashing her an apologetic, sheepish smile, he rounded the VIP partition and headed for the exit.

Seok-joo was completely blasted out of his skull, eyes glazed over, totally oblivious to Jakyeong leaving.

On his way out, Jakyeong casually palmed a pack of cigarettes and a disposable lighter from an unattended table, shoving them into his pockets. Climbing the stairs back to street level, the deafening bass thumping behind him slowly died away. He offered the bouncers at the door a polite nod and strolled down the alleyway in the direction they had come.

As he walked deeper into the district, abandoned houses replaced the storefronts. Not all of them were entirely vacant; here and there, faint yellow light leaked through shuttered windows, accompanied by the muffled drone of television sets.

Reaching a secluded stretch of alley, Jakyeong leaned his back against a cracked brick wall and fished out a cigarette. Sticking it between his lips, he struck the wheel—no flame.

He flicked it again. And again. Nothing.

Out of fluid? He gave the plastic casing a hard shake, but the flint refused to spark.

Ah, ssibal.

Irritated, he hurled the useless lighter onto the asphalt. Of all the damn lighters to swipe...

Disappointed, he chewed lightly on the filter of the unlit cigarette with his front teeth. Just then, faint footsteps rustled from the shadows of an intersecting lane.

Someone leaving their house?

Whoever it was, Jakyeong silently prayed they were a fellow smoker with a working flame. Holding the cigarette between his index and middle fingers, he took a step toward the noise—only for a small, hooded figure to dart out of the dark.

In a split second, the small head slammed right into Jakyeong’s chest. Startled, the figure recoiled, looking up in sheer terror.

It was a young girl with an innocent, youthful face pale with fear. Before Jakyeong could even register the situation, she yanked her ballcap lower over her brow and bolted down the alleyway like a frightened rabbit.

A moment later, an iron gate creaked open nearby. A figure stepped out into the alley, dug through a pile of trash bags, pulled out a small taped parcel, and slipped back inside, locking the gate behind them.

Jakyeong turned on his heel. The silhouette of the young girl was already fading into the distant shadows of another lane.

Snapping the unlit cigarette in half, he tossed it to the ground and began trailing slowly in her direction. Under the sickly yellow glow of the streetlamps, the oversized backpack slung across her thin shoulders looked impossibly heavy.

Gaunt, scrawny limbs. Ragged clothes ill-suited for the weather. Worn-out, scuffed sneakers. And hollow, lifeless eyes that had long since surrendered their soul.

Jakyeong had seen that exact reflection every single morning of his childhood whenever he looked in the mirror.

She was what the underworld called a "mule"—a drop-runner. For clients who couldn't risk buying narcotics out in the open, runners delivered the product secretly, dropping the stash in designated dead-drops and collecting the cash left behind. Syndicate dealers loved using kids for the job for one simple reason: they were cheap, disposable, and easily thrown away when burned.

As he followed her through the dark, the girl's silhouette gradually blurred into the ghost of his own past.

["School? What fucking school?! Stop talking out of your ass and finish your drops, you worthless piece of trash!"]

His father used to beat him bloody over the slightest perceived slight, spewing the same rotten mantra: If you don't want to work, starve to death.

Growing up in that squalor, seeing normal kids his age had shattered his reality. Clean clothes. Shiny shoes. Parents running gentle, loving hands through their hair. He had come home, agonized for days, and finally gathered the courage to ask if he could go to school.

The response was a shower of heavy fists and broken glass.

["I should have aborted you. If I'd just killed you in my womb, my life wouldn't be this cursed!"]

One afternoon, the beating was so severe his shin fractured. With a makeshift wooden splint tied to his leg, he had been forced back out onto the streets to deliver product the very next morning. That day, a demented old customer had tried to sexually assault him in an alley. In the chaos, Jakyeong had lost the payment envelope. When he returned home empty-handed, his mother flew into a violent rage, viciously slapping his swollen face and screaming that he should sell his own body on the corner to pay back the lost money.

He had been ten years old.

"Hold it."

Lost in the suffocating memories of his youth, Jakyeong didn't even notice the steel blade pressing against his ribs until it made contact.

He froze, slowly raising both hands to shoulder height. The assailant said nothing. Turning his torso around with deliberate slowness, Jakyeong found a man of similar height glaring at him beneath a pulled-down cap.

"You a cop?"

Do I look like a cop to you? And if I were a cop, pulling a knife on me would be the dumbest move of your life, wouldn't it?

Jakyeong shook his head meekly.

"Then why the fuck are you tailing the kid?"

The man wore a grubby black windbreaker, a jagged, angry burn scar stretching across the exposed skin of his neck. Even while glaring down Jakyeong, his shifty eyes kept darting down the dark alley where the girl had vanished. The sharp tip of the knife dug a fraction of an inch deeper into Jakyeong’s side, poised to pierce the organ behind it.

"Talk. Why were you following her?"

Hands still raised, Jakyeong pitched his voice into a trembling stammer. "I'm... I'm so sorry... She was just a young kid wandering around alone at night, so I was worried..."

The man narrowed his eyes, scrutinizing him suspiciously. A normal civilian staring down a blade held by a scarred thug would have pissed their pants in terror, yet this kid’s pupils hadn't wavered in the slightest. His mouth was stammering apologies, but his eyes were chillingly dead.

Something was deeply off. The mugger extended his free left hand.

"Wallet."

Jakyeong didn't move.

Should I eliminate him? Or let him live?

Standing at the crossroads of violence, Jakyeong weighed the options while the mugger grew impatient, jabbing the blade forward.

"I said wallet, asshole!"

Right. Let's eliminate him.

The moment Jakyeong resolved to snap the man's windpipe, a sharp shout boomed from the mouth of the alley behind them.

The mugger tucked the knife behind his back instantly, bowing his head in deep deference. Turning around, Jakyeong recognized the man approaching: the thug with the dokkaebi goblin tattoo from the VIP lounge.

Choi Ki-tae flicked his cigarette butt into the puddle and sauntered over with arrogant swagger.

"What's going on here? What's the problem?"

"It's nothing, boss," the mugger stammered hurriedly. "I was just doing my rounds, and this punk was acting suspicious. I was just about to teach him a little lesson—"

SMACK!

Ki-tae’s massive, skillet-sized palm struck the man across the face with explosive force. The mugger stumbled sideways, his boots skidding across the wet asphalt before catching his balance.

Ki-tae’s hand swung back around. SMACK!

"You brainless fuck! Who the hell do you think you're teaching a lesson to?! Who?!"

With every brutal backhand, the man's cheek swelled into a dark, bloody pulp. And with every violent swing of Ki-tae's arm, the goblin tattooed across his bicep contorted into a grotesque, snarling grimace.

Jakyeong’s eyes remained glued to the ink. Goblin tattoos were dime-a-dozen in the Korean underworld, but that specific artistic curvature was unique.

Why does this design look so familiar...?

Jakyeong’s pupils slowly dilated behind his horn-rimmed frames.

Deep in the recesses of his memory, a long-buried image finally clicked into place. He had seen that exact goblin tattoo once before—many years ago.

Translator's Notes (A/N):

  • Dokkaebi (도깨비): Mythological Korean goblins or nature spirits known for their grotesque faces, horns, clubs, and mischievous, sometimes sinister nature. In modern Korean syndicate culture, dokkaebi tattoos are popular motifs representing strength, intimidation, and underworld affiliation.

  • Jige-kkun / Mule (지게꾼): Literally meaning "A-frame carrier" or "porter," jige-kkun is Korean underworld slang for street-level drug couriers or "mules" who deliver illicit goods to dead-drops to insulate the higher-ups from arrest.

  • Ssibal (씨발) & Jjapsae (짭새): Ssibal is Korean for "fuck/shit," while jjapsae is derogatory slang for the police (equivalent to "pig" or "cop").
